purpose: Compare the author fused-old-tail read with the candidate raw-history read under the same represented-token storage budget and original prompt schedule.
method: In a separate author worktree, keep the candidate's 16,384 spatial-plus-insurance budget, protected condition/newest entries, author pending compression, admissions/evictions, indexed RoPE, early-feature prompt and multi-scale anchor. Change the old-tail attention read back to the author's existing fused-history branch while leaving resident pruning disabled. The author's pre-existing reliability weighting in that branch remains part of the control; no new gating, threshold or redetection is introduced. The histories and future token choices can diverge as a consequence of the model's different predictions.
validation: Two label-free seq3 no-op and two fused-window gates must reproduce independently, satisfy every budget/write/pointer check and verify the fused branch actually ran. Two no-inset seq23 short gates must match. Only after these gates, compare full seq23 against the already verified raw-window and cropped original baseline, with ground truth used only for independent audit. Repeat the fused full seq23 run if it produces a noteworthy effect.
limitations: This is a system-level ablation on a selected previously inspected sequence; token selection and propagation histories adapt to the different reads, so it does not isolate attention outputs at a shared state. Stored masks, auxiliary state, pointers, position tensors and transient allocations are outside the spatial token budget.
